newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed higher on Monday but off peaks on profit-taking after bonos rose to a series of all-time records, having vanquished a string of resistance levels, dealers said.

"A profit-taking wave hit the market, but the underlying sentiment remains positive," a dealer said. The Treasury announced a new 10-year bond with a reduced coupon at 7.35 pct from 8.80 pct of the current benchmark which was well received.
The long-term futures contract on Meff reached a record at 111.14 and ended at 110.55, higher than 110.38 where it closed on Friday. Chart analysts put resistance at 111.06.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds, which dipped to 138 basis points but closed wider at 145 bps.

After the October budget deficit data, Budget Secretary Jose Folgado reiterated this morning that the Spanish central government budget deficit would be under 1996 target of 3.5 percent of Gross domestic product.
